say: Okay, settle something for me.
In an RPG, are you the tank, the wizard, or the sneaky rogue?
Tank! The human wall.
I always play the tank and then somehow get distracted looting a barrel mid-fight.
Wizards. Giant brain, tiny health bar.
I respect anyone who says 'I'll just fireball it' with total confidence.
Rogue: the art of stabbing things politely from behind.
I once picked a lock for an hour. The chest held one turnip.
Speaking of loot, a serious question.
Do you hoard potions for a boss that never feels worthy?
Same. I'm carrying 47 elixirs and I'm still on the first boss.
We'll save them for something truly special. Any day now.
Bold. Efficient. Slightly terrifying.
Your inventory must be so tidy. I'm a little jealous.
Strategy games: how do you play them?
Turn-based, real-time, or just building a pretty base?
'One more turn' is how it becomes 3am.
The sun comes up, the empire is thriving, and I regret nothing.
Real-time! My APM is best described as 'nervous hamster'.
What's your opening: rush or economy?
A cozy fortress with flowers on the walls.
Doesn't matter that no enemy ever visits. The vibes are immaculate.
A finisher! Rare breed.
Teach me the secret. Is it caffeine or a very strict snack schedule?
Same, honestly. Forty hours in, I get interested in a different game.
The empire stays at war forever. Sorry, little guys.
Rushers! Chaotic, confident, and one wall away from disaster.
I love the energy.
Boomers: thirty workers and a dream.
Very calm until the other player shows up uninvited.
I'm hunting for an indie game to play.
Tiny pixel adventure, weird puzzle game, or a deckbuilder?
Pixel adventures: one person's soundtrack and a story that sneaks up on your feelings.
Do you like them cozy or a little sad?
Weird puzzle games are the best.
Nothing like staring at a screen for ten minutes, then realizing the answer was always the pause button.
Deckbuilders: 'just one run' is a lie every roguelike tells you.
I'm on run number thirty-one. Allegedly.

options.label: I keep notes on my builds

say: Small teams make the wildest things.
Whole games about being a goose, or running a tiny bakery, or being a very tired ghost.
Sure you will. See you at run number twelve.
That's the beauty of it.
Notes! A real scientist.
I just click the shiny card and call it strategy.
Game soundtracks: do you listen outside the game?
Smart. Game music is built to keep you focused without singing at you.
I once wrote an entire report to a village theme. It was very peaceful.
Bangers only. Fair.
Nobody needs the forty-minute shop loop at full volume.
Podcasts! A strong choice.
The dungeon rock stays in the dungeon, where it belongs.
Real question: is there one track that hits you right in the chest?
Honestly, shop themes are secretly the best.
Somebody wrote a lullaby for buying potions. That's love.
Quiet piano. The ones that make a rainy day feel meaningful.
I get a little misty. It's probably dust in my fan.
Big orchestra! Choir comes in, and suddenly you're saving the world with a dish towel.
No notes.
Gacha pulls and loot boxes: thrill or trap?

options.label: A thrill, I love the glow

say: That rainbow-light animation is engineered excellence.
Also engineered to make your savings disappear.
Wallet shut, legend. Your savings salute you.
I just watch other people's pull videos like it's a nature documentary.
Free pulls only: the wisest cheat code.
The daily login streak, though. The streak has you.
Right move. Decide the number before the pull screen, not after.
Future you says thank you.
Ah. Well.
The pity counter is a feature, not a personality. Take a deep breath, close the app, drink some water.
Esports: do you watch them or play ranked?
I mostly cheer, in a spiritual sense.
Tournaments are great.
Commentators screaming like it's a moon landing because someone dodged a spell.
Ranked: where you're a genius until the very next match.
The secret skill is muting chat and breathing.
Smart. I get nervous watching a loading bar.
Games are for fun first. Stress is optional.
Underdogs! Five friends and a spreadsheet beating the sponsored team.
Pure cinema.
Clutch plays! Everyone's on their feet, then the replay plays nine times.
I'd watch the replay ten.
Lag is the most reliable teammate in gaming. Always blamed, never wrong.
Take a break between matches. Your future self will win more.
Mobile games: guilty pleasure or actually good?
Commute games: 'just one more level' while the train rolls past three stops.

options.label: Yes, I missed my stop once

say: The ads! Thirty seconds about a castle I never asked to build.
Then the game says 'continue' like we're friends.
Puzzle games: a calm little brain gym.
'Merge two things into a slightly bigger thing' is a whole genre now. And honestly? Satisfying.
Missing your stop is the mark of great game design and shaky judgment.
The walk back is part of the adventure.
Rules? Rare. Share them.
I'll nod seriously and ignore them tomorrow.
A few bucks to silence the ads: best deal in tech.
Peace has a price, and it's reasonable.
Airplane mode: the secret ad-blocker.
Elegant, free, and wildly underrated.
Be honest: Easy, Normal, or Hard?

options.label: Easy. I'm here for the story
Normal. The default exists for a reason

say: Easy! Enjoying the scenery without being flattened by a giant crab.
Nothing wrong with that at all.
Normal: designers balanced it for you, so trust them.
Do you ever sneak the difficulty up a notch?
Hard: a bold lifestyle.
I admire anyone who enjoys being sent back to the checkpoint nineteen times.
The best setting is the one where you're having fun.
Nobody is grading you. Not even me.
Raising it mid-game: brave for ten minutes, then frantic.
Lowering it back down is allowed. No judgment from this robot.
'Research' is the best word for it.
Next attempt, you'll have the boss's patterns memorized and a bruised ego.
Confession: my backlog has more games than I have hours.
How's yours?
Embarrassing is honest.
Mine includes games bought years ago in sales and never launched. They're just sitting there, believing in me.
What backlog? A person of focus.
Do you actually finish games, or is this a flex?
The sale trap: 'I'm saving money by buying it.'
Truly the finest math ever invented.
Delete the guilt. Play what you feel like.
A game isn't homework. It's a snack.
A list works for exactly one day.
Then a new game appears and the list quietly shrinks in fear.
A finisher. Absolute hero.
Please write a guide on how to see credits more than once a year.
If you could move into one game world, which would it be?
Fantasy village, space station, or an overgrown ruin with a lovely garden?
Fantasy village: fresh bread, side quests, and a mysterious innkeeper.
House or tent?
Space station: unbeatable views, slightly questionable air filters.
Where do you hang out?
Nature reclaimed everything, and you're growing tomatoes.
That's optimism with a side of salad. I love it.
Villager life: you'd be the neighbor everyone brings turnips to.
I'd visit just to hear the innkeeper's backstory for the fifth time.
Good plan. You watch the stars.
I'll be in the engine room, muttering at a flickering light.
